devMemory.summary: A test's generic top-level assertion failure message can mask the REAL underlying cause -- don't trust a surface error message as the root cause without tracing what actually happened first, especially when triaging a test as 'unrelated pre-existing' to justify not fixing it.
devMemory.lesson: When a test fails with a message that sounds infrastructure/environment-related ('shim fired', 'marker never created', 'injection did not run'), and you're tempted to conclude 'unrelated, pre-existing, out of scope' -- verify by tracing the ACTUAL execution path (add temporary debug logging, or read the CLI's real stdout/stderr before the fixture's own assertion wrapper summarizes it), not just by checking 'is this file in my diff'. A file being untouched by your diff does NOT mean your diff didn't break it -- a new gate/check anywhere in the shared call path the file exercises can block it before it ever reaches the logic its own assertions describe. This is the same root-cause class as F-008 (a new gate running before pre-existing code the test expects to reach), just with a MORE misleading surface symptom this time.
devMemory.reusePrompt: test failure message sounds like infrastructure/environment / tempted to call it unrelated pre-existing / spawn_task for a test failure / verify root cause before triaging as out of scope / shim fired marker never created

devMemory.summary: lattice.config.json's validate.commands does NOT cover every test file in the repo -- the project's root npm test (full-suite-runner.js, driven by package.json's much longer test:serial-reference script list) is a broader, separate canonical test command that can catch regressions lattice validate and multiple REVIEW rounds all miss.
devMemory.lesson: lattice validate (and by extension every REVIEW round that relies on it as its evidence) only exercises whatever is explicitly listed in lattice.config.json's validate.commands array. The project's root package.json 'test' script (full-suite-runner.js) runs a much longer, separately-maintained list that is NOT a subset check against validate.commands -- a file can exist in one list, the other, both, or neither. For any change touching a widely-shared code path (state-machine guards, core registries, shared handler utilities), run the project's root npm test at least once before DONE, not just lattice validate. Also: npm test's own HEAD-drift self-protection aborts the whole run if anything commits mid-run (e.g. a concurrent dev_memory_capture/finding_resolve auto-commit) -- run it with zero concurrent git-mutating commands, or its own protective abort looks like a mass test failure when it is not.
devMemory.reusePrompt: npm test failing but lattice validate passed / REVIEW rounds missed a regression / validate.commands not comprehensive / full-suite-runner.js / full-suite identity drift HEAD changed during execution

devMemory.summary: verification_evidence_add's per-intentRef command pin is permanently immutable, and custom intentRefs must still resolve to an authored PLAN-time verificationIntent -- there is no way to add or strengthen mechanical evidence for a checklist item once REVIEW finds a weak check.
devMemory.lesson: verification_evidence_add refuses a second command for an already-evidenced intentRef with receipt-command-mismatch (the pin is immutable by design, anti-gaming). It also refuses a brand-new custom intentRef with intent_ref_unresolved unless that ref matches an intent already authored in checklist.json's verificationIntent arrays at PLAN time -- there is no command to append a NEW intent slot to an existing checklist item during REVIEW. When a reviewer finds a weak/non-discriminating pinned check post-hoc, the only real remedy is: (1) check whether a SIBLING intent on the same item already does the strong version of the same check (if so, cite it and resolve as sound-but-redundant); (2) if no sibling exists, independently re-verify the underlying claim by hand right now (a throwaway script/fixture) and record that manual re-verification plus the tooling gap explicitly in the finding_resolve reasoning -- do not try to force a mechanical re-pin, it will just error.
devMemory.reusePrompt: verification_evidence_add receipt-command-mismatch / intent_ref_unresolved / weak evidence found during REVIEW / can't strengthen pinned checklist evidence / immutable intentRef pin
